A control with no rows, or equal to the 0% level, stops the run.

nodes.name: Descriptive statistics
nodes.description: n, mean, median, SD, SEM, a t interval of the mean, quartiles (linear, type 7), skewness, excess kurtosis and CV for each column, optionally per group.

nodes.name: Group summary
nodes.description: One row per group: n, mean, SD, SEM, an interval of the mean, and box-plot quartiles, whiskers and notches (matplotlib's rules).

nodes.name: Normality test
nodes.description: Shapiro–Wilk, Anderson–Darling and Lilliefors per group (or per column, with 'columns are groups'), and optionally a KS test against a normal you specify.

nodes.name: Average curves
nodes.description: Line up curves (one per id, such as one per file) on one time grid and average them per group. Curves are interpolated linearly onto the grid, which runs from the latest start, and never extended past their own last time, so n can fall at late times. Two tables: Aligned (every id on the grid) and Mean curves (mean, lower, upper and n at each time). Band (SEM, SD or a t-based 95% CI) sets Mean curves' lower and upper only; a Line plot fed Aligned draws its own error bars or band.

nodes.name: Compare groups
nodes.description: One-way ANOVA (or Welch's, with unequal variances) or Kruskal–Wallis across the groups.

nodes.name: Pairwise comparisons
nodes.description: Compare chosen pairs of groups: t tests, Mann–Whitney, KS, Z-test, permutation, Tukey HSD, Dunn, or Dunnett (each group against a control); or, for the same subjects measured in each condition, paired t or Wilcoxon signed-rank (with a Subject column, or one row per subject).

nodes.name: Compare correlations
nodes.description: Fisher's z test between independent correlations. The input has one row per group with its correlation r and its number of pairs n.

nodes.name: Variance test
nodes.description: Equality of variances: Brown–Forsythe (median-centred Levene), Levene, Bartlett, or the F-test for two groups (group1 variance over group2's).

nodes.name: Effect size
nodes.description: Cohen's d, Hedges' g, Glass's Δ or rank-biserial for chosen pairs, or η² / ω² across all groups, with an optional seeded percentile bootstrap interval.

nodes.name: Adjust p-values
nodes.description: Multiple-testing correction for a column of p-values, for example from several nodes or from outside Bourn. Adds p_adj and reject.

nodes.name: Paired compare
nodes.description: Compare conditions measured on the same subjects: paired t or Wilcoxon signed-rank for two conditions; repeated-measures ANOVA (with Mauchly's test and the Greenhouse–Geisser and Huynh–Feldt corrections) or Friedman for more. One row per subject (choose the condition columns), or a Subject column. RM ANOVA differs from statsmodels where statsmodels is wrong: data with no subject × condition variation give F = ∞ (statsmodels reports rounding noise), and constant data give no result (statsmodels reports F = 0, p = 1).

nodes.name: One-sample test
nodes.description: Test each column or group against a typed value (0, or 1 for a ratio or fold change): one-sample t, or Wilcoxon signed-rank on the differences from the value.

nodes.name: ROC curve
nodes.description: How well a score separates two outcomes: the ROC curve (scikit-learn's points), the area under it with DeLong's standard error and interval, and Youden's best cutoff with its sensitivity and specificity. Two scores measured on the same subjects are compared by DeLong's paired test. Choose the score column (blank is refused: there is no 'every numeric column' here). Differs from scikit-learn where it would mislead: an outcome with one class, or a score that is the same for everyone, is refused (scikit-learn gives no AUC, or 0.5 with no uncertainty); the interval is clipped to 0–1 and says so. Two scores whose difference has no variance (one perfect, the other perfectly reversed) get no z, p or interval.

nodes.name: Contingency table
nodes.description: Pearson's χ², Yates' continuity correction and Fisher's exact test, from two categorical columns or from a table of counts; and McNemar's test for paired yes/no data (the same subjects before and after: two paired columns, one row per subject, or a 2 × 2 count table with the first measurement in rows). McNemar differs from statsmodels where statsmodels is wrong: its continuity correction never passes zero (statsmodels gives b = c a positive χ², and no discordant pair χ² = ∞, p = 0), and the exact test needs whole-number discordant counts (statsmodels checks only their sum).

nodes.name: Agreement
nodes.description: How well two methods or several raters agree. Bland–Altman: bias and limits of agreement between two methods, with their confidence intervals (Bland and Altman 1999), and the paired points. Cohen's kappa (two raters, categories) and weighted kappa (ordered categories, linear or quadratic weights), with SE, Wald interval and the test of κ = 0 (statsmodels' cohens_kappa); Points holds the rater A × rater B counts. ICC: the six Shrout–Fleiss intraclass correlations (named also as McGraw–Wong), each with its F test and interval; Points holds the mean squares. Kappa differs from statsmodels where statsmodels is wrong: at perfect agreement its variance can round below zero and leave the SE and interval empty; here they are 0 and [κ, κ].

nodes.name: Correlation matrix
nodes.description: Pearson, Spearman or Kendall correlations between columns, with p-values, or a distance matrix between columns.

nodes.name: Cluster order
nodes.description: Hierarchical clustering of rows and/or columns: the leaf order for a heatmap and SciPy's linkage rows for a dendrogram.

nodes.name: Linear regression
nodes.description: Ordinary least squares on one or more x columns, or a polynomial in one x, with coefficient tests, fit statistics, residuals and a fitted curve with its confidence band.

nodes.name: Nonlinear regression
nodes.description: Fit a built-in model (4PL, Hill, decays, growth, Michaelis–Menten, Gompertz, logistic, FRAP recoveries) by Levenberg–Marquardt, with parameter tests, dependency, fit statistics and a curve.

nodes.name: Model predict
nodes.description: Predict y from x with a fitted polynomial or nonlinear model, or x from y (inverse, by root finding over a bracket).

nodes.name: Quantify from standards
nodes.description: Fit a standard curve to the standard rows of one table and read every other row's concentration off it, with the dilution applied. Samples outside the standards are kept and flagged: above or below standards (still computed), above the curve (saturated: dilute and rerun) or below the curve (not detected), which have no concentration.

nodes.name: Two-way ANOVA
nodes.description: Two factors with their interaction: Type II (treatment coding) or Type III (sum-to-zero coding) sums of squares, and the cell means.

nodes.name: ANCOVA
nodes.description: Compares groups after adjusting for one or more numeric covariates (e.g. a baseline measurement): the ANCOVA table with Type II (treatment coding) or Type III (sum-to-zero coding) sums of squares, which give the same group and covariate tests here and differ by Type III's intercept row; the adjusted means (each group's prediction with every covariate at its mean, emmeans' estimated marginal means) with SE and interval; and the homogeneity-of-slopes test (group × covariate), which the adjusted comparison assumes (statsmodels' ols with anova_lm and get_prediction). Differs from statsmodels where it would mislead: a constant covariate, one that only differs between the groups, or one collinear with another is refused by name (statsmodels fits them through its pseudo-inverse and reports full-df F tests for an effect it cannot estimate), and a slopes test whose model cannot give each group its own slope is left out with the reason (statsmodels reports it with too many df); and the fits run on the centred value and centred, scaled covariates, so a covariate with a large offset or a tiny spread keeps its digits (statsmodels' fit of the raw columns makes the group F 5.5 times wrong at an offset of 3·10⁷).

nodes.name: MANOVA
nodes.description: Compares groups on several outcome columns at once, optionally adjusted for numeric covariates (MANCOVA): Pillai's trace, Wilks' lambda, the Hotelling–Lawley trace and Roy's largest root for the group and for each covariate, each with its F approximation, df and p (Roy's F is an upper bound, so its p is a lower bound); the test chosen is listed first. Optionally each outcome's own ANOVA (ANCOVA with covariates) for the group, with a multiple-testing correction over the outcomes (statsmodels' MANOVA.mv_test). Differs from statsmodels where it would mislead: the columns are centred and scaled and the statistics taken from a symmetric eigenproblem, so large offsets, very different scales and small effects keep their digits (statsmodels raises or returns a wrong table there); an outcome that is constant, explained exactly by the group, or a linear combination of the others is refused by name (statsmodels quietly tests fewer dimensions), as is a model with fewer residual degrees of freedom than outcomes; a group with no more rows than outcomes is computed with a warning (its own covariances cannot be checked; Pillai's trace is the most robust there); there is no intercept row.

nodes.name: Mixed-effects model
nodes.description: A linear mixed model with one grouping factor: fixed effects, a random intercept and optionally a random slope (REML or ML).

nodes.name: PCA
nodes.description: Principal components: variance explained, eigenvectors, loadings and scores.

nodes.name: Two-way comparisons
nodes.description: Follow a Two-way ANOVA: each group against another within every level of the other factor (simple effects), and whether those differences change between levels (interaction contrasts), with the model's pooled error or each pair's own.

nodes.name: FRAP fit
nodes.description: Fit FRAP normalize's recovery curve from the bleach on: one exponential, two exponentials, or free diffusion into a circular spot (Soumpasis 1983). Mobile fraction, t½, rates, D, R² and adjusted R², every model's scores side by side, and the full-scale curve. The fractional recovery (how much came back by the end of the recording) is read from the data for every curve; a model that cannot be fitted leaves its numbers empty and says why. To draw the fit over the whole curve, connect Fitted curve to XY line's Overlay.

nodes.name: Survival analysis
nodes.description: Kaplan–Meier curves with Greenwood log(−log) intervals, the log-rank test across groups, and pairwise log-rank tests with a correction.

nodes.name: Cox regression
nodes.description: Hazard ratios for time-to-event data: a Cox proportional hazards model of time and event (1 = event, 0 = censored) on numeric and categorical covariates (each level against a reference level), with Efron's or Breslow's handling of tied times and optional strata, each with its own baseline hazard. Reports each coefficient with its SE, Wald z and p and the hazard ratio with its interval, and the likelihood-ratio, Wald and score tests of all covariates together (statsmodels' PHReg). Differs from PHReg where it would mislead: a covariate that orders the events perfectly, or a level with no events, has no finite hazard ratio and is refused by name (PHReg warns and returns a huge coefficient); a constant or collinear covariate and data without events are refused in words (PHReg returns garbage or crashes); covariates are centred and the fit is unit-free, so a column far from zero or in tiny units keeps every digit (PHReg loses them).

nodes.name: Outlier detection
nodes.description: ROUT (Prism's robust nonlinear method, or its fast version) at a false discovery rate Q, or iterative two-sided Grubbs at alpha, per group.

nodes.name: Power / sample size
nodes.description: Plan a study: give three of effect size, n, alpha and power and get the fourth, for a one-sample, paired or two-sample t test, a one-way ANOVA (Cohen's f, n the total) or two proportions (Cohen's h from p1 and p2, normal approximation), as statsmodels' power classes. n is given unrounded and rounded up, with the power the rounded n reaches; the curve shows power against n. No input table. nodes.description: Test each column or group against a typed value (0, or 1 for a ratio or fold change): one-sample t, or Wilcoxon signed-rank on the differences from the value.

nodes.name: ROC curve
nodes.description: How well a score separates two outcomes: the ROC curve (scikit-learn's points), the area under it with DeLong's standard error and interval, and Youden's best cutoff with its sensitivity and specificity. Two scores measured on the same subjects are compared by DeLong's paired test. Choose the score column (blank is refused: there is no 'every numeric column' here). Differs from scikit-learn where it would mislead: an outcome with one class, or a score that is the same for everyone, is refused (scikit-learn gives no AUC, or 0.5 with no uncertainty); the interval is clipped to 0–1 and says so. Two scores whose difference has no variance (one perfect, the other perfectly reversed) get no z, p or interval.

nodes.name: Contingency table
nodes.description: Pearson's χ², Yates' continuity correction and Fisher's exact test, from two categorical columns or from a table of counts; and McNemar's test for paired yes/no data (the same subjects before and after: two paired columns, one row per subject, or a 2 × 2 count table with the first measurement in rows). McNemar differs from statsmodels where statsmodels is wrong: its continuity correction never passes zero (statsmodels gives b = c a positive χ², and no discordant pair χ² = ∞, p = 0), and the exact test needs whole-number discordant counts (statsmodels checks only their sum).

nodes.name: Agreement
nodes.description: How well two methods or several raters agree. Bland–Altman: bias and limits of agreement between two methods, with their confidence intervals (Bland and Altman 1999), and the paired points. Cohen's kappa (two raters, categories) and weighted kappa (ordered categories, linear or quadratic weights), with SE, Wald interval and the test of κ = 0 (statsmodels' cohens_kappa); Points holds the rater A × rater B counts. ICC: the six Shrout–Fleiss intraclass correlations (named also as McGraw–Wong), each with its F test and interval; Points holds the mean squares. Kappa differs from statsmodels where statsmodels is wrong: at perfect agreement its variance can round below zero and leave the SE and interval empty; here they are 0 and [κ, κ].

nodes.name: Correlation matrix
nodes.description: Pearson, Spearman or Kendall correlations between columns, with p-values, or a distance matrix between columns.

nodes.name: Cluster order
nodes.description: Hierarchical clustering of rows and/or columns: the leaf order for a heatmap and SciPy's linkage rows for a dendrogram.

nodes.name: Linear regression
nodes.description: Ordinary least squares on one or more x columns, or a polynomial in one x, with coefficient tests, fit statistics, residuals and a fitted curve with its confidence band.

nodes.name: Nonlinear regression
nodes.description: Fit a built-in model (4PL, Hill, decays, growth, Michaelis–Menten, Gompertz, logistic, FRAP recoveries) by Levenberg–Marquardt, with parameter tests, dependency, fit statistics and a curve.

nodes.name: Model predict
nodes.description: Predict y from x with a fitted polynomial or nonlinear model, or x from y (inverse, by root finding over a bracket).

nodes.name: Quantify from standards
nodes.description: Fit a standard curve to the standard rows of one table and read every other row's concentration off it, with the dilution applied. Samples outside the standards are kept and flagged: above or below standards (still computed), above the curve (saturated: dilute and rerun) or below the curve (not detected), which have no concentration.

nodes.name: Two-way ANOVA
nodes.description: Two factors with their interaction: Type II (treatment coding) or Type III (sum-to-zero coding) sums of squares, and the cell means.

nodes.name: ANCOVA
nodes.description: Compares groups after adjusting for one or more numeric covariates (e.g. a baseline measurement): the ANCOVA table with Type II (treatment coding) or Type III (sum-to-zero coding) sums of squares, which give the same group and covariate tests here and differ by Type III's intercept row; the adjusted means (each group's prediction with every covariate at its mean, emmeans' estimated marginal means) with SE and interval; and the homogeneity-of-slopes test (group × covariate), which the adjusted comparison assumes (statsmodels' ols with anova_lm and get_prediction). Differs from statsmodels where it would mislead: a constant covariate, one that only differs between the groups, or one collinear with another is refused by name (statsmodels fits them through its pseudo-inverse and reports full-df F tests for an effect it cannot estimate), and a slopes test whose model cannot give each group its own slope is left out with the reason (statsmodels reports it with too many df); and the fits run on the centred value and centred, scaled covariates, so a covariate with a large offset or a tiny spread keeps its digits (statsmodels' fit of the raw columns makes the group F 5.5 times wrong at an offset of 3·10⁷).

nodes.name: MANOVA
nodes.description: Compares groups on several outcome columns at once, optionally adjusted for numeric covariates (MANCOVA): Pillai's trace, Wilks' lambda, the Hotelling–Lawley trace and Roy's largest root for the group and for each covariate, each with its F approximation, df and p (Roy's F is an upper bound, so its p is a lower bound); the test chosen is listed first. Optionally each outcome's own ANOVA (ANCOVA with covariates) for the group, with a multiple-testing correction over the outcomes (statsmodels' MANOVA.mv_test). Differs from statsmodels where it would mislead: the columns are centred and scaled and the statistics taken from a symmetric eigenproblem, so large offsets, very different scales and small effects keep their digits (statsmodels raises or returns a wrong table there); an outcome that is constant, explained exactly by the group, or a linear combination of the others is refused by name (statsmodels quietly tests fewer dimensions), as is a model with fewer residual degrees of freedom than outcomes; a group with no more rows than outcomes is computed with a warning (its own covariances cannot be checked; Pillai's trace is the most robust there); there is no intercept row.

nodes.name: Mixed-effects model
nodes.description: A linear mixed model with one grouping factor: fixed effects, a random intercept and optionally a random slope (REML or ML).

nodes.name: PCA
nodes.description: Principal components: variance explained, eigenvectors, loadings and scores.

nodes.name: Two-way comparisons
nodes.description: Follow a Two-way ANOVA: each group against another within every level of the other factor (simple effects), and whether those differences change between levels (interaction contrasts), with the model's pooled error or each pair's own.

nodes.name: FRAP fit
nodes.description: Fit FRAP normalize's recovery curve from the bleach on: one exponential, two exponentials, or free diffusion into a circular spot (Soumpasis 1983). Mobile fraction, t½, rates, D, R² and adjusted R², every model's scores side by side, and the full-scale curve. The fractional recovery (how much came back by the end of the recording) is read from the data for every curve; a model that cannot be fitted leaves its numbers empty and says why. To draw the fit over the whole curve, connect Fitted curve to XY line's Overlay.

nodes.name: Survival analysis
nodes.description: Kaplan–Meier curves with Greenwood log(−log) intervals, the log-rank test across groups, and pairwise log-rank tests with a correction.

nodes.name: Cox regression
nodes.description: Hazard ratios for time-to-event data: a Cox proportional hazards model of time and event (1 = event, 0 = censored) on numeric and categorical covariates (each level against a reference level), with Efron's or Breslow's handling of tied times and optional strata, each with its own baseline hazard. Reports each coefficient with its SE, Wald z and p and the hazard ratio with its interval, and the likelihood-ratio, Wald and score tests of all covariates together (statsmodels' PHReg). Differs from PHReg where it would mislead: a covariate that orders the events perfectly, or a level with no events, has no finite hazard ratio and is refused by name (PHReg warns and returns a huge coefficient); a constant or collinear covariate and data without events are refused in words (PHReg returns garbage or crashes); covariates are centred and the fit is unit-free, so a column far from zero or in tiny units keeps every digit (PHReg loses them).

nodes.name: Outlier detection
nodes.description: ROUT (Prism's robust nonlinear method, or its fast version) at a false discovery rate Q, or iterative two-sided Grubbs at alpha, per group.

nodes.name: Power / sample size
nodes.description: Plan a study: give three of effect size, n, alpha and power and get the fourth, for a one-sample, paired or two-sample t test, a one-way ANOVA (Cohen's f, n the total) or two proportions (Cohen's h from p1 and p2, normal approximation), as statsmodels' power classes. n is given unrounded and rounded up, with the power the rounded n reaches; the curve shows power against n. No input table. Differs from statsmodels where it would mislead: power uses the noncentral survival function, not 1 − cdf (statsmodels gives 0 for a power below about 1e-16) and has no NaN where statsmodels' power is NaN (SciPy's noncentral t fails past a noncentrality of about 8, e.g. d = 1.19 at n = 93); when the smallest sample (2, or 2 per group) already has the power, that sample is the answer and says so (statsmodels returns e.g. 40 with a convergence warning); Cohen's f above 1 and alpha below 1e-12 are solved (statsmodels raises); an answer statsmodels' fallback accepts without reaching the power (d = 4.94 for 99% at n = 3; the answer is 5.58) is solved exactly. Refused in words: a power not reached with up to 10 million subjects (statsmodels gives e.g. 7.8e8), an effect size of 0, p1 = p2, a one-sided alternative against an effect on the other side, a target power not above alpha, alpha or power outside (0, 1).

versions.description: Collapsible field groups: what to analyse and the method stay open; rarer settings sit in closed groups (Options, Resampling, Curve, Missing values, File format), and fields the chosen setting never reads are hidden. Results are unchanged.

nodes.name: Python Script
nodes.description: Your own Python between nodes: inputs arrive by name as Polars tables and NumPy arrays; assign each output by name. Desktop only.

Western bands: a node that finds lanes and bands on a blot (size-independent detection, a drawn frame or black edge is not a lane, touching lanes split at their dips), names them from a ladder and a loading control, and gives a lane table, groups and the blot; lanes can come from an experiment's gel layout. Canvas and Focus views with zoom and pan and a lane editor under the blot. Western panel: a figure of cropped strips with the uncropped blot, its levels recorded in the method record. Requires bourn.plot 0.8. Describe actions for the assistant; setting descriptions in units.

nodes.name: Read image
nodes.description: Read a TIFF, PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP, AVIF or JPEG 2000 image from your workspace or the shared space. Calibration and bit depth come from the TIFF's ImageJ description, OME-XML or resolution tags (a stack's calibration, recorded on its first page, applies to every page); the other formats are uncalibrated 8-bit (PNG and JPEG 2000 may be 16-bit). The file's own markers say whether it is lossless or lossy, recorded with the image; a lossy or possibly lossy file (JPEG, most WebP and AVIF) adds a warning, as its pixel values are approximations. HEIC is not read. Colour images become three channels, palette images keep their colours, and an alpha channel is dropped. Frames One reads the page or animation frame Page names; All outputs every page or frame as a list, for a loop region, whatever the file holds (a single image gives a list of one).

nodes.name: Read OIR
nodes.description: Read one frame of an Olympus/Evident FluoView OIR file as a multi-channel image, with channel names, LUT colours, 12-bit depth and pixel size from the file. Use Split channels to work on one channel. Channels are numbered as the file numbers them (Loom's reader remapped them). Channel colours can be changed in the channel table; the chosen colours are the output's recorded channel colours.

nodes.name: Split channels
nodes.description: Split a multi-channel image into one image per channel, keeping each channel's name, colour, bit depth, calibration and capture. Channels are known by how they were captured (laser and emission window), so the same dye goes to the same output in every file, wherever the file records it. Outputs Each channel gives one output per ticked channel, named by the table; a file without that channel leaves it inactive and what is wired after it does not run for that file. Outputs List gives the ticked channels the file has as one list named by the table, so a Save's {key} names each file by channel. The table fills from the first image read; a channel it does not have is noted and offered there, never split by itself.

nodes.name: Merge channels
nodes.description: Stack images into one multi-channel image, in the order the connections were made (reorder connections to reorder channels). Every input must have the same size, pixel type and calibration; multi-channel inputs contribute all their channels, at most 8 in total.

nodes.name: Choose channels
nodes.description: Keep, drop and reorder an image's channels and set each one's colour and name. Pixels are copied exactly; only which channels are present and their colours and names change. An empty list keeps every channel as it is. A channel without a colour keeps the one it was drawn in.

nodes.name: Brightness / contrast
nodes.description: Stretch the display window [low, high], in native units of the image's bit depth, to the full range, with an optional midtone gamma. High 0 means the image's full scale (Loom's default of 255 saturated 12- and 16-bit images). The result is a unit-scale image; every channel is stretched the same way.

nodes.name: Multi-channel brightness / contrast
nodes.description: Per-channel display windows (Synapse's Multi-Channel B&C): each channel is stretched from its low to its high value onto the unit scale and takes the colour chosen for it, or white when it is shown gray. Ranges are [low, high] or [low, high, gamma] per channel in native units, with high 0 meaning full scale; missing entries use the full scale. A channel with no colour chosen keeps the input's. Synapse took up to four separate channel inputs; here merge channels first.

nodes.name: Gamma contrast
nodes.description: gain × pixel^gamma on the unit scale (scikit-image adjust_gamma). Not clipped: a gain above 1 can exceed full scale, as in Loom.

nodes.name: CLAHE
nodes.description: Contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalisation (scikit-image equalize_adapthist) with tiles of an eighth of each side (scikit-image's default), each channel on its own. Clip limit 0 means no clipping. Loom's tiles and its handling of colour (per channel, or only the HSV value) depended on which backend ran; Bourn always uses scikit-image's tiles, per channel.

nodes.name: Rolling ball background
nodes.description: Subtract a rolling-ball background (scikit-image rolling_ball) of the given radius in pixels, per channel, clipping at zero.

nodes.name: RGB to gray
nodes.description: Reduce a colour image to one channel: Rec.601 or Rec.709 luminosity, the channel average, or one channel. A single-channel image passes through; a fourth channel (alpha) is ignored.

nodes.name: HSV range mask
nodes.description: Mask the pixels of a colour image whose hue (degrees), saturation and value (percent) fall inside the ranges, inclusive; a hue range with min above max wraps through red. Exclude inverts the mask. Also outputs the image with everything outside the mask black.

nodes.name: Colour deconvolution
nodes.description: Separate histology stains (scikit-image separate_stains) with a scikit-image preset or an ImageJ Colour Deconvolution 2 matrix, completing a two-stain matrix by Ruifrok's rule or a cross product. Each output is the stain reconstructed in its own colour, or with Grayscale on, its density normalised to its maximum.

nodes.name: Bit depth convert
nodes.description: Declare a different acquisition bit depth. The pixel fractions are unchanged, as in Loom; what changes is how native-unit parameters downstream (thresholds, display windows, histograms) map onto them.

nodes.name: Set scale
nodes.description: Set the pixel size in micrometres, either directly or from a known distance and its length in pixels (which takes precedence when both are given). Pixels are unchanged.

nodes.name: Image math
nodes.description: Add, subtract, multiply or divide two images of the same size on the unit scale; division by zero divides by one. Not clipped, as in Loom. A single-channel image combined with a multi-channel one applies to every channel.

nodes.name: Colorize channel
nodes.description: Tint each channel with a colour and sum them into an RGB image, clipped to full scale. A single-channel image takes the first colour (Loom spread one channel over all three colours, turning it white); the channel colours are recorded, so the composite is reproducible.

nodes.name: Merge images
nodes.description: Blend any number of images by per-pixel sum, mean, maximum or minimum, clipped to full scale. Smaller images are placed at the top left of the largest, so mean and minimum include that zero padding, as in Loom. If any input has colour, all are treated as RGB.

nodes.name: Resize
nodes.description: Resize to a target size (optionally fitting inside it with the aspect ratio kept) or by a scale factor, with bicubic interpolation and anti-aliasing when shrinking (scikit-image resize, order 3). The pixel size is scaled on each axis. Masks are resized nearest-neighbour and stay binary.

nodes.name: Rotate
nodes.description: Rotate counter-clockwise by an angle in degrees, enlarging the canvas to fit and filling with black, with bicubic interpolation (scikit-image rotate, resize on; Loom used SciPy's equivalent). Masks rotate nearest-neighbour and stay binary.

nodes.name: Mirror / flip
nodes.description: Flip left-right (horizontal), top-bottom (vertical) or both.

nodes.name: Crop
nodes.description: Keep the rectangle starting at (x, y) with the given width and height, clipped to the image. A rectangle entirely outside the image is an error (Loom returned an empty image). The crop's origin is recorded in the result's provenance.

nodes.name: Mask crop
nodes.description: Crop to the bounding box of a mask, expanded by padding and clipped to the image, optionally blacking out pixels outside the mask. Without a mask the image passes through; an empty mask is an error.

nodes.name: Binary threshold
nodes.description: Mask the pixels brighter than the threshold, in native units of the image's bit depth (40 on a 12-bit image is 40/4095), or with Invert the pixels at or below it. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Multi-channel threshold
nodes.description: Threshold every channel of a multi-channel image on its own, in native units, and combine the enabled channels' masks with AND or OR. Thresholds are per channel [threshold, above (1) or below (0), enabled (1/0)]; missing entries are [128, 1, 1]. Also outputs every channel's mask and the image with the combined mask applied.

nodes.name: Local threshold
nodes.description: Mask pixels brighter than their neighbourhood's Gaussian-weighted mean (scikit-image threshold_local, block size odd, reflect border). Colour images use the channel mean. An even block size is rounded up.

nodes.name: Multi-Otsu
nodes.description: Split intensities into classes by multi-level Otsu (scikit-image threshold_multiotsu, 256 bins) and output the class map: 0 for the darkest class up to classes - 1. Loom emitted a coloured picture of the classes; the class map is the data, and every preview colours it. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Gaussian blur
nodes.description: Gaussian blur of the given sigma in pixels, each channel on its own (scikit-image gaussian: nearest border, truncated at 4 sigma). Synapse's default sigma was 10.

nodes.name: Median filter
nodes.description: Median over a square window of the given odd size, each channel on its own (reflect border).

nodes.name: Convolve
nodes.description: Convolve each channel with a kernel given as rows of numbers (SciPy ndimage convolve, reflect border); with Normalise the kernel is divided by its sum.

nodes.name: White top-hat
nodes.description: Bright details smaller than a disk: image minus its opening, each channel on its own.

nodes.name: Black top-hat
nodes.description: Dark details smaller than a disk: the closing minus the image, each channel on its own.

nodes.name: Bandpass filter
nodes.description: ImageJ-style ideal FFT band-pass keeping structures between the small and large sizes in pixels, clipped to [0, 1] (Large 0 keeps every large structure). As in Loom and Synapse the cut-offs are measured against the image width on both axes and the mean is removed. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Frangi vesselness
nodes.description: Frangi vesselness for bright ridges over integer sigmas from min to max (scikit-image frangi, reflect border), normalised to its maximum. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Canny edges
nodes.description: Canny edges (scikit-image canny) after a Gaussian of the given sigma. Thresholds are gradient magnitudes in native units of the bit depth; 0 uses 10% and 20% of full scale. (Loom compared unscaled values to a [0, 1] gradient, so any threshold of 1 or more found no edges.) Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Sobel edges
nodes.description: Sobel gradient magnitude, rescaled to [0, 1]. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Prewitt edges
nodes.description: Prewitt gradient magnitude, rescaled to [0, 1]. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Laplacian edges
nodes.description: Laplacian of a Gaussian of the given sigma, shown around 0.5: zero crossings are 0.5, the strongest response of either sign reaches 0 or 1. Colour images use the channel mean.

nodes.name: Erode
nodes.description: Erode a mask with a disk of the given radius, pixels beyond the edge counting as background. This is Loom's native behaviour; Synapse (and Loom without its native module) iterated a 3×3 cross instead.

nodes.name: Dilate
nodes.description: Dilate a mask with a disk of the given radius, pixels beyond the edge counting as background. This is Loom's native behaviour; Synapse (and Loom without its native module) iterated a 3×3 cross instead.

nodes.name: Open
nodes.description: Erosion then dilation, each iterated with a 3×3 cross (SciPy binary_opening, background beyond the edge): removes thin protrusions and specks.

nodes.name: Close
nodes.description: Dilation then erosion, each iterated with a 3×3 cross (SciPy binary_closing, background beyond the edge, so foreground touching the edge is eroded, as in Loom): fills thin gaps.

nodes.name: Fill holes
nodes.description: Fill background regions not connected to the image edge (SciPy binary_fill_holes, 4-connected background).

nodes.name: Remove small objects
nodes.description: Remove connected regions whose area is at most the maximum size in pixels (scikit-image 0.26 remove_small_objects). Connectivity 1 is 4-connected, 2 is 8-connected; the default follows Loom (1), where scikit-image's own default and Synapse differ. Synapse's default size was 500.

nodes.name: Remove small holes
nodes.description: Fill holes whose area is at most the maximum size in pixels (scikit-image 0.26 remove_small_holes). Connectivity 1 is 4-connected, 2 is 8-connected. Synapse's default size was 50.

nodes.name: Distance ring mask
nodes.description: The band of background within a distance (pixels, Euclidean) of the mask; with Include original the mask itself is added, giving a dilated mask.

nodes.name: Skeletonize
nodes.description: Thin a mask to one-pixel lines (scikit-image skeletonize, Zhang's method), then optionally prune: each round removes every endpoint, shortening all open branches by one pixel. Loom also offered Lee's method, which is not ported.

nodes.name: Medial axis
nodes.description: The medial axis of a mask (scikit-image medial_axis, tie-breaks from a fixed seed so the result is reproducible) and the distance to the background along it, in pixels. Loom output a coloured picture of that distance; here it is the distance itself, zero off the axis.

nodes.name: Skeleton analysis
nodes.description: Measure each 8-connected skeleton piece: centroid, length (orthogonal steps 1, diagonal steps √2, so loops and junctions count every pixel pair, as in Loom) and junction pixels (three or more neighbours), after dropping pieces with fewer pixels than the minimum. Also outputs the junctions dilated by a disk, the pieces as labels, and a picture of skeleton (gray) and junctions (red). Lengths are in pixels.

nodes.name: Keep max intensity region
nodes.description: Keep the one 8-connected region of a mask with the largest summed intensity, among the N largest regions by area (Synapse; Loom's version was disabled). Colour images use the channel mean. An empty mask gives an empty mask.

nodes.name: Connected components
nodes.description: Number each connected region of a mask 1, 2, ... in raster order; 4- or 8-connected.

nodes.name: Clean labels
nodes.description: Drop regions touching the image edge and/or keep only the N largest (ties to the lower id), then renumber the survivors 1..N in their original order.

nodes.name: Watershed
nodes.description: Split touching objects in a mask: markers at the peaks of the distance transform at least the given distance apart (8-connected), flooded over the inverted normalised distance inside the mask (scikit-image watershed). Click on the preview to add seeds and Shift-click to remove one; each added seed starts its own object, and a removed automatic seed stays removed (the one nearest the click, within half the separation). Untick Automatic seeds to place every seed by hand. Objects closer to the image edge than the separation get no automatic seed (as in scikit-image); add one by hand. Outputs the labels, a table of region measurements in pixels, and the seeds used, one per automatic marker.

nodes.name: Particle select
nodes.description: Keep the regions that pass every rule, such as area ≥ 50 and circularity > 0.6; rules on an unknown column are ignored and no rules keep everything. Outputs the kept regions as a mask and as labels with their original numbers.

nodes.name: Particle toggle
nodes.description: Keep the regions within the area limits (pixels; 0 means no limit) that are in the selection; an empty selection keeps every region within the limits. Click regions in the preview to toggle them. Outputs a mask and labels with their original numbers.

nodes.name: Particle classify
nodes.description: Assign regions to named groups (click regions in the preview, Shift-click to unassign). Outputs labels whose values are group numbers (1 for the first group, 0 unassigned) and a table of every region's area, centroid and group.

nodes.name: Blob detection
nodes.description: Find bright round spots by Laplacian of Gaussian (scikit-image blob_log, 10 scales between the radii, overlap 0.5, border blobs kept). The threshold is a LoG response on the unit scale. Colour images use the channel mean. Outputs a table y, x, radius_px and an overlay with the blobs circled.

nodes.name: Find contours
nodes.description: Trace iso-contours at a level given as a fraction of full scale (0.5 traces a mask's edges) with scikit-image find_contours, largest area first. Outputs the contours drawn closed into a mask and a table of contour_id, x, y points. No contour gives an empty mask and table (Loom raised an error).

nodes.name: Hough lines
nodes.description: Straight lines through a mask's pixels (scikit-image hough_line over 180 angles, then hough_line_peaks with the threshold a fraction of the strongest vote). Outputs an overlay with the lines drawn edge to edge and a table theta (rad), rho (px), x0, y0, x1, y1.

nodes.name: Hough circles
nodes.description: Circles through a mask's pixels for every integer radius from min to max (scikit-image hough_circle and hough_circle_peaks, threshold a fraction of the strongest vote). Outputs an overlay and a table cx, cy, radius.

nodes.name: Hough ellipse
nodes.description: Ellipses through a mask's edge pixels (scikit-image hough_ellipse; its cost grows with the cube of the edge-pixel count, so use it on edges or small masks). Keeps up to N ellipses whose votes reach the threshold fraction of the best, strongest first. Outputs an overlay and a table cx, cy, a, b, orientation (rad).

nodes.name: Region measurements
nodes.description: Measure every region: area, centroid, box (bottom and right exclusive), perimeter, circularity, shape and orientation (degrees), in pixels. Regions are the 8-connected parts of the mask, or the given labels (then the mask is ignored). With an intensity image, adds mean, sum, max and min intensity on the unit scale (luminance for RGB) and the weighted centroid. Min area drops smaller regions from the table and the labels.

nodes.name: Image stats
nodes.description: One row of statistics. For a mask: image size, area and area fraction, and the shape of all its pixels taken as one region. For an image: mean, population std, min, max and median of the channel mean on the unit scale, inside the mask when one of the same size is given, and with Per channel the same for every channel of a colour image.

nodes.name: GLCM texture
nodes.description: Haralick texture of the channel mean quantised to the given levels (truncating): the gray-level co-occurrence matrix at one distance over 0°, 45°, 90° and 135° (scikit-image graycomatrix, normed), with contrast, dissimilarity, homogeneity, energy, correlation and ASM averaged over the angles.

nodes.name: Intensity profile
nodes.description: Intensities along a line drawn on the preview, sampled bilinearly at about one point per pixel of length, every channel on the unit scale. With no line drawn, the middle half of the centre row (the line the preview starts with). Outputs a table of distance (px) and one column per channel.

nodes.name: Image histogram
nodes.description: Pixel counts over the image's bit-depth range in equal bins (at most one per value), inside the mask when one of the same size is given. Outputs Bin_Lower, Bin_Upper in native units and a count column per channel (Intensity for one channel).

nodes.name: Colocalization
nodes.description: Colocalisation of two channels on the unit scale: Pearson, Spearman and Kendall (Kendall on a fixed random 50,000-pixel sample of larger sets), Manders' overlap coefficient, M1 and M2 above each channel's Otsu threshold, and Li's ICQ. Over the mask when given; with labels, one row per region.

nodes.name: Mask overlay
nodes.description: Draw a mask on an image: an optional translucent fill and an outline of the given width just inside the mask edge (the mask minus its erosion by a 3×3 cross; width 0 draws no outline). Loom passed a mismatched mask through silently; here it is an error. Synapse's outline is centred on the edge and styled.

nodes.name: Label overlay
nodes.description: Colour each labelled region on an image: a translucent fill and a boundary of the given width in the region's colour (scikit-image find_boundaries, thick). Label L takes colour L of the palette, repeating.

nodes.name: Scale bar
nodes.description: Draw a calibrated scale bar of the given length in µm, with its length written above it, in a corner. Needs a calibrated image (set scale or a reader that records it). On the preview's Draw tab, drag the bar to move it to a corner and drag its end to change the length.

nodes.name: ROI mask
nodes.description: Draw regions of interest on the preview: ellipses, rectangles, pen outlines and freehand lassos, each a region you can reshape, resize, rotate or move, and a brush and eraser that add pixels to a region or take them away. Outputs every region together as a mask, and the image cropped to it with everything outside set to 0 (untick Crop to region to keep the full size). With nothing drawn, an empty mask and the image unchanged. For one label per region, follow it with Connected components.

nodes.name: Draw shape
nodes.description: Annotate an image for figures: rectangles, ellipses, polygons and arrows drawn on the preview (click a shape again to rotate it), each with its own line colour, width, style, fill and label, and text placed with a click, over the outlines of any connected masks and labelled regions. Outputs an 8-bit RGB picture.

nodes.name: Mask editor
nodes.description: Edit a mask by drawing on the preview: rectangles, ellipses, polygons, lasso, brush and flood fill, each added, subtracted, intersected, XOR-ed or replacing. The edits are kept as a list and replayed on the input mask, so they survive upstream changes. In Cells mode every cell is its own layer (cells may overlap) and the output is one mask per non-empty cell, in cell order.

nodes.name: Label editor
nodes.description: Paint labelled regions on the preview: rectangles, ellipses, polygons, lasso, brush and flood fill, each painting its label number (Union or Replace) or clearing it (Subtract). Edits are replayed on the input labels. Outputs the labels and a table of each label's area in pixels.

nodes.name: Box annotator
nodes.description: Draw, move, resize and rotate labelled bounding boxes on the preview, starting from optional proposals (a table xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, class_name, confidence) and a class catalogue (a table id, name, color). Every box needs a class before the node completes; a box whose geometry or class was edited loses its confidence. Put it in a review region to pause a run for annotation.

nodes.name: Western bands
nodes.description: Measure a western blot scan: finds the lanes, the band rows, the ladder and the tilt, then gives each lane's band volumes for the proteins you name (each by its expected size, as target or loading control), their ratio to the loading control and the fold change over the lanes you choose. An RGB scan is read as the mean of its channels. Volumes are in arbitrary units (x100). Every number carries its flags (saturated, faint); proteins that match no band are listed, never guessed. Outputs the table (one row per sample lane), the cleaned-up blot with lanes, boxes and sizes drawn on it, and each lane's profile.

nodes.name: Western panel
nodes.description: The publication figure of a blot from Western bands' Blot: one strip per protein row, cut from the picture Western bands measured, with lane labels from its lane table, protein names and sizes, and a line at every splice. Also the uncropped blot with each crop boxed, for the supplement. Brightness and contrast are black and white points per whole strip and are written to the method record; the numbers never see them. Both outputs are vector figures (text stays text) for Compose figure and Save figure.

nodes.name: Cell edge mask
nodes.description: FiloQuant step 1: the cell body. Pixels at or above the threshold (native units of the bit depth; the mean of the first three channels), holes filled, then opened n times (erode, then dilate, 3×3 square, edges padded) and optionally opened again.

nodes.name: Filopodia detect
nodes.description: FiloQuant step 2: thin protrusions. Optional CLAHE, a 5×5 sharpen, two 3×3 medians, a threshold in native units, objects under 8 px removed, and only elongated objects kept (circularity 4πA/P² at most 0.8, Crofton perimeter). With a cell mask and a distance, only detections within that many pixels of the cell are kept.

nodes.name: Filopodia analyze
nodes.description: FiloQuant step 3: detections outside the cell, smaller objects removed, gaps closed, thinned (Zhang), and every connected skeleton measured as one filopodium (diagonal steps count √2). Also measures the cell edge length. Lengths in pixels, and in µm when either mask is calibrated, each step weighted by its direction when pixels are not square.

nodes.name: Crop cells
nodes.description: Cut each cell out of an image: the bounding box of each cell mask plus a margin, clipped to the image. Neighbouring cells inside the box are kept. Outputs the image crops and the mask crops as two lists in the same order, for a loop over cells; empty masks are skipped.

nodes.name: Filopodia cell summary
nodes.description: One row per cell from a Filopodia analyze table: the count, mean and total length, the edge length, and the density (filopodia per µm of edge when calibrated, else per px, stated in density_unit; Synapse did not record which).

nodes.name: Save image
nodes.description: Write an image as PNG or TIFF to a granted save location. One channel (uint8, uint16 or float32; float32 needs TIFF) is written exactly, pixels unchanged. Two or more channels, including an ordinary RGB picture, are written as the 8-bit RGB composite a result preview shows by default (each channel in its colour, on its bit-depth scale, not auto-contrasted). To keep raw per-channel values, use Split channels and save each channel. TIFF keeps the micrometre calibration.

nodes.name: Read time-lapse
nodes.description: Read a whole time-lapse, an Olympus/Evident .oir file or a TIFF stack, as one item: every frame of the channels chosen (every channel when Channels is empty), each frame's time in seconds, the pixel size, and the bleach (stimulation) frame when the .oir records it. A TIFF's pages are its frames; its interval comes from the ImageJ or OME description. A typed Interval replaces the file's times with an even grid. The stack's size in memory is limited to 2 GB. In a batch, each video's stack stays in working storage while the run lasts, so a batch of large videos may need working storage raised in settings.

nodes.name: Split channels
nodes.description: Split a several-channel time-lapse into one time-lapse per channel, each keeping every frame's time, the bleach frame, the pixel size and the channel's capture. Channels are known by how they were captured (laser and emission window), so the same dye goes to the same output in every file. Outputs Each channel gives one output per ticked channel, named by the table; a file without that channel leaves it inactive and what is wired after it does not run for that file. Outputs List gives the ticked channels the file has as one list named by the table, so a Save's {key} names each file by channel.

nodes.name: Save time-lapse
nodes.description: Write a time-lapse to a granted save location; the file name's extension picks the format. TIFF (.tif) keeps every frame exactly, pixels unchanged, as an ImageJ stack: Fiji and Read time-lapse open it with its frame interval, pixel size and the preview's brightness. Uneven frame times are written as their mean interval, and the bleach frame is not kept. MP4 (.mp4) and GIF (.gif) are the video as the preview plays it, 8-bit, for slides and talks: MP4 plays in PowerPoint, QuickTime and Windows players; GIF loops. They can carry a scale bar and a time stamp (from the bleach, or the first frame), dragged into place on the preview. For viewing, never for measuring.

nodes.name: FRAP normalize
nodes.description: FRAP regions' intensities as a recovery curve: background subtracted, then double normalized (bleached ÷ reference, each over its pre-bleach mean) or single (bleached only), so the pre-bleach level is 1. Checks the bleach depth and gap ratio (easyFRAP-web's, under 0.6 is flagged). The curve runs from before the bleach (negative times) to the end: for a figure of the whole curve, XY line with Mark at x 0.

nodes.name: FRAP regions
nodes.description: Draw the bleached spot, a reference region in the cell and a background region on a time-lapse, then measure each one's mean on every frame. Each region is one outline you draw and reshape, with brush and eraser marks that add to it or cut from it. The bleached region can follow the spot, the others stay in place or move between frames drawn by hand. Bleach frame 0 takes the file's or finds the largest drop; Interval 0 takes the file's frame times. In a loop, each video keeps its own regions and stops until drawn.

versions.notes:
The former `bourn-align` sample plugin, renamed and grown into Bourn's sequence plugin. It is a clean break: workflows
saved with `bourn-align`'s nodes (`align.read`, `align.kalign`, `align.save`) are not migrated; their nodes are now
`sequence.read`, `sequence.align` and `sequence.save`. The Sequence viewer (`plot.alignment`) keeps its id.

- Read sequences reads a plain text file (a Sanger read) as one sequence named after the file; one sequence per line
  is the explicit format "lines".
- Sequence sets may carry a type per row; Align refuses a set of mixed types, and a name with two sequences, naming them.
- New: Sequences (a typed or pasted reference library and collector) and Sequence selection (the wanted stretch of a
  read, matched against the references by bourn_sequence_native).
- Sequence selection writes its proposal and every candidate (identity, coverage, rank, which was proposed) to its outputs
  (`Match`, `Candidates`), so review shows what the node proposed and the run record says why a reference was picked.
- A held review choice that no longer matches the read, the references or the Output (or is off the codons of its frame
  when the output is protein) refuses the item in words; it is never replaced by the proposal. When no reference is clearly
  ahead the best match's stretch is proposed, with the reference left unpicked.
- Read sequences types each record by its letters: a file mixing DNA and protein is a mixed set with a type per row.

Clearer descriptions for the Align, Read, Save, Select and Table nodes and the Sequence viewer's parameters. No change to
what any node computes.

nodes.name: Read sequences
nodes.description: A FASTA file, or a plain text file (a Sanger read) as one sequence named after the file, as a table of name and sequence.

nodes.name: Sequences
nodes.description: Name, sequence and type of each row, typed or pasted as FASTA. Wired sets join the rows; identical rows collapse to one, and one name with two different sequences is a conflict that Align refuses. Use it before a loop as the reference library and after it as the collector.

nodes.name: Sequence selection
nodes.description: The wanted stretch of a read. Matched against the references it proposes the reference, strand, frame and stretch, running through stop codons to where the match ends; with none it proposes the longest open reading frame. Confirm or adjust it in review. Output sets DNA, RNA or protein, or follows the reference.

nodes.description: A multiple sequence alignment with Kalign 3. Gap penalties at 0 take the mode's own; threads at 0 take Kalign's default.

nodes.description: Save an alignment as FASTA, Clustal (.aln), Stockholm (.sto) or PHYLIP (.phy), from the extension.

nodes.description: Sequences or an alignment as a figure: coloured residues, consensus and conservation, labels. Open it in Focus mode to zoom, recolour and label; Use this view sets what it outputs.

versions.notes:
Bourn Sheets, a spreadsheet tool on the Tools tab (D227). A workbook is a Bourn record: readable JSON is what is kept,
with every saved version listed.

- A grid (IronCalc) with formulas, number formats, merges and frozen panes; English and Traditional Chinese.
- Import an `.xlsx` or a `.csv` (UTF-8, or UTF-16 with its mark); what a workbook cannot keep is listed on import.
  Export `.xlsx`, or one sheet as `.csv` (UTF-8 with a mark, values only).
- One person edits a workbook at a time; others see it read-only with the editor's name.
- The Read sheet node reads a range of one saved version of a workbook into a table.
- A workbook is at most 8 MB.

versions.notes:
A workbook made from a file is that file plus your changes (Sheets file trail; not published).

- Record format 2: a link to the source file (its place, fingerprint and name) and only the cells, sheets and styles
  that differ from it, each edited cell with the value it had. A workbook started empty holds its own cells as before;
  format 1 workbooks keep opening as workbooks started empty.
- New actions to open a workbook from a file, tell whether the file is unchanged, changed or gone, save only the
  changes, point a workbook at a file again and drop edits.
- Removed the import and export actions: an import copied the file and an export left no record.
- The page opens a workbook from a file (picked or dropped), shows whether the file is unchanged, changed or gone (a compare view for a changed file, nothing applied until chosen), lists your changes and the history, saves as a file through a recorded run, and lists each workbook's source and the workflows that use it.
- New **Sheet** node: a file and a workbook's changes, as one sheet's table and as a workbook. The edits apply to the
  file they were made to; another file with the same layout runs only a layer of formulas and labels (a value typed
  for plate1 is never written into plate2: the run refuses and names both files). Input the formulas do not reach and
  source sheets the file lacks are warned, never dropped silently. A run never writes the saved workbook, and states
  the workbook revision, the file's fingerprint and what was edited as facts a recipe keeps.
- New **Save workbook** node: a workbook (or chosen sheets) to .xlsx, or one sheet to .csv, through the write door.
- Read sheet reads a workbook that holds its own cells, and says so when a workbook reads a file (use the Sheet node).
- Records of format 2 are not readable by 0.1.0.
